issue.title: Bob web-clip (Chrome/Skia) PDFs fragment words in PDFKit, so Highlights quotes come back split

task_type_fields.impact: Every web article captured with `bob ref create <URL>`, plus every `URL %` capture and gkeep URL ingest, produces a PDF whose Highlights quotes can contain split or merged words. The damage flows into ref-note Highlights sections and annotation-derived follow-up tasks. The earlier web-URL research named this as an unverified risk and as the gating Mac test (research:202610/web_url_reference_pdf_capture/web_url_reference_pdf_capture__final.md §3.4/§6.4). This probe confirms that the Bob template does not avoid it. Candidate fixes: re-typeset `article.json` through xelatex or Typst (both read back at 0 % in the same probe), or find a Chromium-side mitigation (turning kerning off did not help).
task_type_fields.location: scripts/web_clip/web_clip_render.py (Chromium page.pdf with template/reader.css) — the web-article route of bob ref create
task_type_fields.repro:
**Reproduction (2026-10-15, MacBook, macOS 26.5 PDFKit):**

1. Copy production Bob web-clip PDFs (HeadlessChrome 154 / Skia, rendered with `scripts/web_clip/template/reader.css`) to the Mac, for example `~/bob/lib/blogs/introducing_omnigent_meta_harness_combine_control_and_share_your_agents.pdf` and `~/bob/lib/blogs/harness_engineering.pdf`.
2. Build a reference vocabulary from MuPDF's extraction of the same file: `mutool draw -q -F txt -o - <pdf> > <pdf>.vocab.txt`. MuPDF extracts these files cleanly, so the probe measures only PDFKit-specific damage.
3. Run `swift pdfkit_probe.swift <pdf>.vocab.txt <pdf>`. The script is attached to the research report at `obsidian_note_pdf_snapshots__cld_assets/spike/pdfkit_probe.swift`. It selects every line with `PDFSelection.selectionsByLine()` and counts words that are not in the vocabulary.

**Results:**

| PDF | Words | Not in vocab | Rate | Examples |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| omnigent web clip (Bob template) | 1207 | 77 | 6.38 % | `mnigen`, `agen ts` |
| harness_engineering web clip (Bob template) | 3326 | 213 | 6.40 % | `agen`, `wi th` |
| xelatex `create`-route PDF (`lib/chat/agent_catalog_pane.pdf`) | 7027 | 0 | 0.00 % | — |
| Spike Chrome print with `font-kerning: none; letter-spacing: 0` | 920 | 22 | 2.39 % | `bl ocked`, `pr oject` |

Real Highlights output agrees. `lib/blogs/introducing_omnigent_meta_harness_combine_control_and_share_your_agents.md` contains quotes such as `AP` / `Is`, `decisionsFor example`, and `git pushor`.

issue.creation_reason: Found while researching note PDF rendering: a Mac PDFKit probe shows production Bob web-clip PDFs come back with about 6.4% of words split. That damages Highlights quotes and annotation tasks for every web capture, while xelatex PDFs read back clean.

evidence.note: Independent impact evidence from real Highlights quotes on athena (master 8a3c561, 2026-10-15). For every ref note with highlights, quote words were checked against poppler's text of the same PDF. Chrome/Skia PDFs whose body fonts embed as Type 3 (5 docs, Bob reader template with variable woff2, e.g. steve_kinney_agent_memory, omnigent, gastown_readme): 88/1631 = 5.4% damaged, all intra-word splits (ublished, spectru, ueue, ultiple). Chrome/Skia PDFs whose fonts embed as CID TrueType (15 Mac-printed docs using static Helvetica Neue/Georgia/Menlo): 18/1643 = 1.1%, zero intra-word splits, only line/code-span join merges (intervalmust, callsase). pandoc+xelatex: 3/1558 = 0.19%. Skia emits Type 3 for variable fonts and CID TrueType for static TrueType, even within one PDF (lib/blogs/build_with_muse_code.pdf). Bob ships only *-wght-*.woff2 variable fonts (src/scripts.rs include_bytes!), so every web clip is Type 3. Likely fix: serve static TTF faces in reader.css, check pdffonts shows no Type 3, then rerun the PDFKit probe. A ~1% line-join merge residue may remain. Script and output: research 202610/area_project_note_reading_pdfs/area_project_note_reading_pdfs__final_assets/. The cld probe asset this bead cites moved to 202610/area_project_note_reading_pdfs/obsidian_note_pdf_snapshots__cld_assets/spike/pdfkit_probe.swift.
